:::{#exm-sigma-algebra}
#### $\sigma$-algebras for die rolls

For the die rolls $D = \set{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}$ ([sets of die rolls](sets-functions.qmd#exm-set)),
the collection of all subsets of $D$ is a $\sigma$-algebra on $D$,
since complements and unions of subsets of $D$ are again subsets of $D$.
So is the smaller collection

$$\set{\emptyset, \set{2, 4, 6}, \set{1, 3, 5}, D}$$

which contains $D$,
the complement of each of its sets,
and every union of its sets:
for example, $\set{2, 4, 6} \cup \set{1, 3, 5} = D$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-not-sigma-algebra}
#### A collection that is not a $\sigma$-algebra

The collection $\set{\emptyset, \set{1}, D}$ is not a $\sigma$-algebra on $D = \set{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}$:
it contains $\set{1}$ but not its complement $D \setminus \set{1} = \set{2, 3, 4, 5, 6}$.

:::
